candidates.hypothesis: In mm/memory.c and mm/zswap.c / mm/swap_state.c, allowing high-order folios (orders 2 and 4) when all swap slots in the aligned cluster range reside in zswap enables assembling contiguous compressed swap slots into a single high-order folio during swap-in and installing with a single set_ptes() hold, eliminating repeated PTL acquisition and per-page fault overhead while preserving latency and memory stability. Reject if candidate causes data corruption, slot leakage in zswap, page table locking races, fails correctness gates, or fails calibrated screening.

mechanism.claim: In mm/memory.c (thp_swapin_suitable_orders) and mm/zswap.c (zswap_load), when all swap slots in an aligned order-2 or order-4 range reside in zswap, thp_swapin_suitable_orders permits the high-order folio and zswap_load assembles contiguous compressed slots into the allocated high-order folio, installing them in do_swap_page with a single set_ptes() call under one page table lock hold.
mechanism.falsifier: Exact-tree review shows lost lifetime protection, incorrect slot conflict handling, or broken cache lookup fallback. Correctness, metadata spread <1%, and calibrated fast-tier screen independently gate execution.

state.reason: Adds zswap contiguous presence check and multi-subpage folio decompression dispatch in swap-in path.

lifetime.reason: High-order folios allocated with standard GFP flags and locked/unlocked under page table lock.

locking.reason: Single set_ptes hold retains PTL once per batch instead of per-page acquisition.

error_paths.reason: Falls back cleanly to order-0 single swapin if any slot is missing or allocation fails.

configuration.reason: Transparently active when mTHP and zswap are enabled without new user configuration.

decision.complexity_justification: Allowing high-order folios to assemble contiguous compressed zswap slots eliminates repeated PTL acquisitions and fault overhead, but introduces contiguous residency checking and multi-subpage decompression logic.
decision.frontier_reason: First validated batched high-order mTHP swap-in implementation for zswap with full 17-gate correctness proof and calibrated screening.

upstream_comparison.reason: Frozen line declares no relevant upstream comparison.

decision.reason: Candidate achieves FAST_PASS with measured latency reductions (-4.7% sequential mean, -5.8% sequential p99 on zram-64k) and passes all scored guardrails across all 4 screening pairs.
decision.learning_value: Demonstrates that assembling contiguous compressed zswap entries into high-order folios (orders 2 and 4) successfully avoids repeated page table lock holds and delivers noticeable latency improvements on zswap, but the geometric mean effect (-2.3%) remains within the calibrated noise floor (+/-6.2%), indicating that batched swap-in alone does not overcome compression latency without asynchronous readahead.

reasons: benefit does not justify added complexity
